caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1049 of 1999
lawyer:
Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record - For the Petitioner. 
Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record - For Respondent Nos. 1 and 2. 
Not represented - Respondent No. 3.
parties:
Sooraya Rahman ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Hajee Md Elias and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Amin Chowdhury CJ: This petition for leave to appeal is against judgment and order dated 10-6-1999 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 120 of 1982 dismissing the appeal and upholding the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 1012 of 1980 dismissing the suit. 

 2. The short fact leading to this petition is that Title Suit No. 186(A) 78 was filed by the plaintiff-petitioner for securing a decree for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property stating, inter alia, that respondent No. 1 is the owner of the suit property and respondent No. 2 is the son and attorney of respondent No. 1. This respondent No. 2 being an attorney entered into a contract with the plaintiff petitioner for transferring? property having a three-storied building, thereon on 15-1-1973 at a consideration of Taka 2,01,500 and at the time of execution of deed of agreement a sum of Taka 50,000 was paid as part payment of the consideration which was duly acknowledged in the agreement. Part possession of the suit property was delivered to the plaintiff where he is still in possession. As per agreement defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were to obtain income tax, gain tax certificate and permission from the Dhaka Improvement Trust, now RAJUK, but only the DIT clearance was obtained but they failed to obtain income tax, gain tax clearance certificates. By the time the petitioner purchased the stamp papers for execution and registration of the sale deed and after preparing the same it was not handed over to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for affixing their signatures with the stamp paper but retained the same with them till filing of the suit. Thereafter, the plaintiff through his Advocate served a notice and offered balance amount of Taka 1,51,500 but the defendant denied to perform the contract which resulted in filing of the present suit. 

 4. Before the trial Court both the parties adduced evidence in support of their respective cases. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the evidence on record by judgment and decree dated 19-5-1982 dismissed the suit. Thereafter, the petitioner moved the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 120 of 1982 and a Division Bench of that Division after hearing both the parties by judgment dated 10-6-1999 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 6. It appears that the High Court Division thoroughly considered the facts and circumstances of the case and came to the finding that the contract has been frustrated and that the suit as framed is not maintainable as DIT, now RAJUK, though a necessary party has not been impleaded in the suit. The High Court Division found that defendant No. 1 is only a lessee for 99 years and the property belongs to DIT and there is a provision in the lease deed that permission from DIT would be necessary for transfer of the property. In the instant case permission was obtained initially but in the suit DIT was not made a party which made the suit bad for defect of parties. The High Court Division on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record found that the contract was ultimately frustrated by the action of the plaintiff and, as such, no decree can be passed and accordingly, affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. We have considered the submission made by the learned Advocate and also gone through the judgment of the trial Court as well as of the appellate Court and we hold that no illegality and wrong has been committed by the High Court Division in dismissing the appeal.
